findings.text: A newcomer learns within the first two sentences what Athena is, and the next paragraph explains that this page is a sample study. The opening does its job.
findings.source: Athena is an open-source system, written in Rust, that turns a short request into a change to a code repository.

findings.text: The next step is stated near the top and repeated under Next steps with direct repository links. A newcomer knows where to go.
findings.source: Next step: install Athena or read firstmate itself

findings.text: The page promises these Athena features but never shows any of them: no request, no checker, no costs. A newcomer has to take the main selling points on trust.
findings.source: It shows how it read the request, has one AI model do the work and a different one check it, and records what each step cost.

findings.text: This tells the newcomer why the page matters. But after the opening, almost all of the page is about firstmate's internals, so someone who came to learn about Athena gets two short paragraphs and then a long technical walkthrough of a different tool.
findings.source: Athena made this study of firstmate to show that it can read an unfamiliar project and explain it with every statement traced to a claim, and every claim to lines in the project's own files.

findings.text: The 'What firstmate is' section explains the studied project in plain words, so the sample is easy to follow even without knowing firstmate.
findings.source: Firstmate is a tool for people who direct AI coding agents. It keeps a backlog of programming tasks and hands each one to a worker

findings.text: The 'Words used first' list uses 'secondmate' before defining it. The glossary also leaves 'in scope' explicitly undefined, which adds jargon for a first-time reader.
findings.source: home — A firstmate home is the place that holds a backlog of tasks. A secondmate is a persistent home of its own, not a task in someone else's backlog.

findings.text: The yolo, green and red merge rule is repeated in nearly the same words at least six times across the start section, the transition cards and the glossary. That repetition makes a long page longer without adding anything.
findings.source: With yolo on, firstmate merges green work that is in scope itself, and never a red one.

findings.text: The Counters entry and the transition cards refer to each other by bare IDs such as t1 and c31, with no links between them. A newcomer has to scroll back and forth to match them up.
findings.source: places-held, changed by transitions t1, t3, t4, t9, t11

findings.text: The findings list skips f2 without saying why, which may make a careful reader wonder whether something was left out.
findings.source: Limits of this study: f1 ... f3 ... f4

findings.text: Every claim links to exact lines at a pinned commit. That shows in a concrete way the traceability the opening promises, and it is the page's strongest evidence for Athena's value.
findings.source: Check a statement: follow a bracketed claim id to the claim, then its source link to the file and lines in firstmate at the pinned commit.
